q: A can complete a work in 15 days and B can complete it in 20 days. How many days will they take together?
exp: Combined rate = 1/15 + 1/20 = 7/60. Therefore time = 60/7 days.

q: A can complete a work in 18 days. What fraction of the work does A complete in 6 days?
exp: Work completed = 6/18 = 1/3.

q: If 8 workers complete a work in 10 days, how many worker-days are required?
exp: Worker-days = 8 × 10 = 80.

q: A worker earns ₹2,400 for 8 days. What is his daily wage?
A pipe fills a tank in 12 hours. What fraction of the tank does it fill in 3 hours?
exp: Work done = 3/12 = 1/4 of the tank.

q: A pipe fills a tank in 6 hours and another pipe fills it in 3 hours. How long will they take together?
exp: Combined rate = 1/6 + 1/3 = 1/2. Therefore time = 2 hours.

q: A can complete a work in 10 days. B takes twice as long as A. How many days will B take?
exp: B takes twice A's time, so B takes 20 days.

q: A can complete a work in 24 days. How many days will he take to complete 3/4 of the work?
exp: Time required = 24 × 3/4 = 18 days.

q: A and B work at the same efficiency. If A takes 14 days to complete a work, how many days will B take?
exp: Equal efficiency means equal completion time, so B takes 14 days.

q: A pipe fills a tank in 20 hours. How long will it take to fill one-fourth of the tank?
exp: One-fourth of the work requires 20 × 1/4 = 5 hours.

q: If 12 workers complete a work in 5 days, how many worker-days are required?
exp: Total worker-days = 12 × 5 = 60.

q: A receives ₹900 for 3 days of work. What is his daily wage?
exp: Daily wage = 900 ÷ 3 = ₹300.

q: A can complete a work in 16 days and B in 8 days. How many times is B as efficient as A?
exp: B takes half the time, so B is twice as efficient as A.

q: A pipe fills a tank in 15 hours. How much of the tank is filled in 5 hours?
exp: Work completed = 5/15 = 1/3.

q: A completes a work in 5 days and B completes it in 10 days. How much work do they complete together in one day?
exp: Combined work = 1/5 + 1/10 = 3/10.

q: A can complete a work in 12 days and B in 16 days. How many days will they take together?
exp: Combined rate = 1/12 + 1/16 = 7/48. Time = 48/7 days.

q: A and B together can complete a work in 9 days. A alone takes 15 days. How many days will B alone take?
exp: B's rate = 1/9 - 1/15 = 2/45. Therefore B takes 45/2 = 22.5 days.

q: A can complete a work in 20 days and B in 30 days. If they work together for 6 days, what fraction of the work remains?
exp: Combined rate = 1/20 + 1/30 = 1/12. In 6 days they complete 1/2, leaving 1/2.

q: A can complete a work in 15 days. B is 50% more efficient than A. How many days will B take?
exp: B's efficiency is 1.5 times A's. B's time = 15/1.5 = 10 days.

q: A is 20% less efficient than B. If B completes a work in 16 days, how many days will A take?
exp: A's efficiency is 80% of B's. A's time = 16/0.8 = 20 days.

q: A and B together can complete a work in 12 days. If A alone takes 20 days, how many days will B alone take?
exp: B's rate = 1/12 - 1/20 = 1/30. Hence B takes 30 days.

q: A can complete a work in 24 days and B in 36 days. They work together for 8 days. What fraction of the work remains?
exp: Combined rate = 1/24 + 1/36 = 5/72. In 8 days they complete 5/9, leaving 4/9.

q: A works for 4 days on a job that he can complete in 16 days. B then completes the remaining work in 9 days. In how many days could B complete the whole work alone?
exp: A completes 4/16 = 1/4, so B completes 3/4 in 9 days. Full work takes 9 × 4/3 = 12 days.

q: A can complete a work in 18 days and B in 12 days. A works alone for 6 days. How many more days will B need?
exp: A completes 6/18 = 1/3. Remaining = 2/3. B takes (2/3) × 12 = 8 days.

q: A and B together can complete a work in 8 days. A alone takes 24 days. How many days will B alone take?
exp: B's rate = 1/8 - 1/24 = 1/12. Therefore B takes 12 days.

q: A pipe fills a tank in 10 hours and another pipe fills it in 15 hours. How long will they take together?
exp: Combined rate = 1/10 + 1/15 = 1/6. Therefore time = 6 hours.

q: A pipe fills a tank in 12 hours and a leak empties it in 18 hours. If both are open, how long will the tank take to fill?
exp: Net rate = 1/12 - 1/18 = 1/36. Therefore the tank fills in 36 hours.

q: A pipe fills a tank in 8 hours and a leak empties it in 24 hours. If both are open, how long will the tank take to fill?
exp: Net rate = 1/8 - 1/24 = 1/12. Therefore the tank fills in 12 hours.

q: Two pipes can fill a tank in 20 minutes and 30 minutes respectively. How long will they take together?
exp: Combined rate = 1/20 + 1/30 = 1/12. Therefore time = 12 minutes.

q: A pipe fills a tank in 6 hours. With a leak open, it takes 9 hours. How long would the leak alone take to empty the tank?
exp: Leak rate = 1/6 - 1/9 = 1/18. Hence the leak alone empties the tank in 18 hours.

q: Four workers complete a job in 18 days. How many days will 6 workers take, assuming equal efficiency?
exp: Total work = 4 × 18 = 72 worker-days. Six workers need 72/6 = 12 days.

q: Ten workers can complete a work in 12 days. After 4 days, two workers leave. How many more days will the remaining workers need?
exp: Total work = 120 worker-days. Work done in 4 days = 40. Remaining = 80. Eight workers need 10 more days.

q: Six workers can complete a work in 15 days. After 5 days, three additional workers join. How many total days are required?
exp: Total work = 90 worker-days. First 5 days complete 30. Remaining 60 is completed by 9 workers in 60/9 = 6⅔ days. Total = 11⅔ days.

q: A and B receive ₹5,000 for a job. A works for 6 days and B for 4 days at the same daily wage. What is A's share?
exp: Wages are proportional to days. A's share = 6/(6+4) × 5000 = ₹3,000.

q: Three workers work for 5, 6 and 9 days respectively at equal daily wages. If the total wage is ₹4,000, what is the third worker's share?
exp: Total days = 20. Third worker's share = 9/20 × ₹4,000 = ₹1,800.

q: A can complete a work in 25 days and B in 15 days. If they work together for 5 days, what fraction of the work remains?
exp: Combined rate = 1/25 + 1/15 = 8/75. In 5 days they complete 8/15, leaving 7/15.

q: A can complete a work in 30 days and B in 20 days. They work together for 4 days, then B leaves. How many more days will A need?
exp: Together rate = 1/30 + 1/20 = 1/12. In 4 days they complete 1/3. Remaining = 2/3. A needs (2/3) × 30 = 20 days.

q: A and B together complete a work in 15 days. A alone takes 25 days. How many days will B alone take?
exp: B's rate = 1/15 - 1/25 = 2/75. Hence B takes 75/2 = 37.5 days.

q: A is twice as efficient as B. Together they complete a work in 18 days. How many days will A alone take?
exp: If B's rate is x, A's rate is 2x. Together 3x = 1/18, so A's rate = 1/27. A takes 27 days.

q: A is three times as efficient as B. If B takes 24 days to complete a work, how many days will they take together?
exp: A takes 24/3 = 8 days. Combined rate = 1/8 + 1/24 = 1/6. Therefore they take 6 days.

q: A pipe fills a tank in 16 minutes and B fills it in 24 minutes. If both are opened for 8 minutes, what fraction of the tank is filled?
exp: Combined rate = 1/16 + 1/24 = 5/48. In 8 minutes they fill 40/48 = 5/6, so none of the listed options is correct.

q: A pipe fills a tank in 15 minutes and a waste pipe empties it in 30 minutes. If both are opened for 10 minutes, what fraction of the tank is filled?
exp: Net rate = 1/15 - 1/30 = 1/30. In 10 minutes, 10/30 = 1/3 is filled, so none of the listed options is correct.

q: A worker completes 3/5 of a work in 12 days. How many more days will he need to finish the remaining work?
exp: If 3/5 takes 12 days, the remaining 2/5 takes 12 × (2/3) = 8 days.

q: A can complete a work in 40 days and B in 24 days. If A works for 8 days and B works for 6 days, what fraction of the work is completed?
exp: A completes 8/40 = 1/5 and B completes 6/24 = 1/4. Total = 9/20, so none of the options is exact.

q: A, B and C can complete a work alone in 12, 18 and 36 days respectively. How many days will they take if all work together?
exp: Combined rate = 1/12 + 1/18 + 1/36 = 1/6. Therefore they take 6 days.

q: A and B together can complete a work in 12 days. A is 50% more efficient than B. How many days will A alone take?
exp: Let B's rate be x and A's rate 1.5x. Thus 2.5x = 1/12, so A's rate = 1/20. A takes 20 days.

q: A can complete a work in 24 days, B in 36 days and C in 72 days. A and B work together for 6 days, then C joins them. How many total days are required?
exp: A+B rate = 1/24 + 1/36 = 5/72. In 6 days they complete 5/12. Remaining = 7/12. All three rate = 1/12. Remaining takes 7 days. Total = 13 days, so none of the options is correct.

q: A can complete a work in 20 days. B is 25% more efficient than A and C is 25% less efficient than A. How many days will all three take together?
exp: Rates relative to A are 1, 1.25 and 0.75. Total rate = 3/20. Therefore time = 20/3 = 6⅔ days, so none of the options is exact.

q: A pipe fills a tank in 12 hours, B in 18 hours, and a leak empties it in 36 hours. If all are opened together, how long will the tank take to fill?
exp: Net rate = 1/12 + 1/18 - 1/36 = 1/9. Therefore the tank fills in 9 hours.

q: Three pipes fill a tank in 12, 15 and 20 minutes respectively. How long will they take if all are opened together?
exp: Combined rate = 1/12 + 1/15 + 1/20 = 1/5. Therefore time = 5 minutes.

q: A and B can complete a work in 10 days, B and C in 12 days, and C and A in 15 days. How many days will all three take together?
exp: Adding pair rates gives 1/10 + 1/12 + 1/15 = 1/4. This is twice the combined rate, so all three together work at 1/8 per day and take 8 days.

q: A can complete a work in 18 days and B in 24 days. They work together for 6 days, then B leaves. How many more days will A need?
exp: Together they complete 6 × (1/18 + 1/24) = 7/12. Remaining = 5/12. A needs (5/12) × 18 = 7.5 days.

q: Eight workers can complete a work in 18 days. After 6 days, three workers leave. How many more days will the remaining workers need?
exp: Total work = 8×18 = 144 worker-days. Work done in 6 days = 48. Remaining = 96. Five workers need 96/5 = 19.2 days.

q: A is 50% more efficient than B, and B is 20% more efficient than C. If C takes 36 days to complete a work, how many days will A take?
exp: B's efficiency is 1.2 times C's. A's efficiency is 1.5 times B's = 1.8 times C's. Therefore A's time = 36/1.8 = 20 days.
